I am 65 years old and I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and I know what N-P-K means, but mostly I go by what I have done before and what the neighbors do. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, so I can buy the inputs I need, but fertilizer is expensive now and I still count every yuan.

The wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October after rotary tilling the whole field. I used an improved variety, Jimai 22, same as last year because it stood up well and did not fall over. For the base fertilizer I put down 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 16-16-16 kind from the dealer. Now that spring is here, I will topdress with 30 kg per mu of urea at the jointing stage, and if the leaves look a little light I will add another 5 kg per mu at booting. Last year I only used 25 kg per mu of urea and the wheat turned a bit yellow, so this year I will not skimp. I have a good well, so I will irrigate four times: the winter irrigation I already did, then one at green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once in early spring, insecticide once when the aphids show up, and fungicide once if the weather gets humid. I expect about 520 kg per mu if no big disaster hits.

For the summer maize, after I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid seed. I buy new hybrid seed every year from the input shop — I do not save seed anymore because the hybrid gives me at least 100 kg more per mu. I will use no-tillage, just plant right after the wheat harvest like everyone else around here; there is no time to plough and the wheat straw I chop and spread. At sowing I put 30 kg per mu of compound fertilizer in the seed furrow, and at the big trumpet stage I spread 30 kg per mu of urea. I will irrigate twice: once if June is dry after sowing, and once at tasseling. I spray herbicide once before the corn comes up, and insecticide once for the corn borer. I expect about 600 kg per mu from the maize.

My household has seven people and we need both crops to do well. The wheat we eat as flour and sell some; the maize we sell to the grain buyer. I have to think about the whole budget — if I spend too much on the wheat fertilizer, I have less for the corn, but I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved.
